title: Benchmarking factor methods
text: small benchmark loop, varying signal strength:
code: bench_one <- function(effect, seed) {   s <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 45, effect = effect, seed = seed)   r <- run_factor_pipeline(s$data, methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "JIVE"), k = 3,                            verbose = FALSE)   cl <- cluster_results(r, k = 3, include_data = FALSE)   out <- compare_clusterings(cl, setNames(s$metadata$group,                                           s$metadata$sample))$vs_truth   out$effect <- effect   out } grid <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 1.5, 2, 3), function(e)   do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(sd) bench_one(e, sd))))) agg <- aggregate(ARI ~ method + effect, grid, mean) library(ggplot2) ggplot(agg, aes(effect, ARI, colour = method)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_colour_manual(values = factomics_palette(3)) +   labs(x = "Group effect size", y = "Mean ARI (3 replicates)",        title = "Group recovery as signal increases") +   theme_factomics()

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: RABFA (Zhang, Chang, Shen Long, 2024, Biometrics) Bayesian factor model uses prior knowledge features act together, typically pathway graph KEGG, guide loadings shrunk zero: every loading Laplace shrinkage parameter, strong signals shrunk little noise lot (adaptive shrinkage); log shrinkage parameters features connected graph correlated sparse precision matrix learnt data, connected features tend selected together, edges disagree data -weighted (robust wrong edges). factomics implements Gaussian version model Gibbs sampler (Metropolis-Hastings shrinkage parameters, block Gibbs graph precision matrix), written published model. graph data frame edges columns , adjacency matrix, one adjacency matrix per view. Feature names may plain (TP53) view-prefixed (rna::TP53); edges different views ignored, paper. build graph simulation actually used, connecting features loaded true factor: result usual scores loadings (posterior means) , meta, loadings whose 95% credible interval excludes zero, posterior shrinkage parameters, BIC-type criterion, log-likelihood trace checking convergence:  well selected loadings match true signal features? Without pathway knowledge, build_feature_graph() gives data-driven graph (features view high correlation), rabfa() shortcut: main tuning parameters (rabfa_control()) nu1 (overall shrinkage; larger sparser) nu2 (adaptive loading’s shrinkage ); paper chose , k, grid search BIC stored meta$bic. eta = 10 eps = 0.2 follow paper. MCMC needs enough iterations: paper used 5,000-10,000; check loglik_trace flattened burn-.
code: W <- sim$truth$W pathways <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(W), function(v)   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(W[[v]])), function(f) {     on <- rownames(W[[v]])[W[[v]][, f] != 0]     data.frame(from = on[1], to = on[-1], view = v)   # star-shaped pathway   })))) edges <- data.frame(from = paste0(pathways$view, "::", pathways$from),                     to   = paste0(pathways$view, "::", pathways$to)) head(edges, 3) #>                      from                      to #> 1 transcriptome::gene_001 transcriptome::gene_002 #> 2 transcriptome::gene_001 transcriptome::gene_015 #> 3 transcriptome::gene_001 transcriptome::gene_035 res_rabfa <- run_factor_pipeline(sim$data, methods = "RABFA", k = 4,                                  rabfa_graph = edges,                                  rabfa_iter = 1500, rabfa_burnin = 750,                                  verbose = FALSE) res_rabfa$RABFA$meta$n_edges #> [1] 181 m <- res_rabfa$RABFA$meta colSums(m$selected) #> F1 F2 F3 F4  #> 66 62 62  0 plot(m$loglik_trace, type = "l", xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Log-likelihood",      main = "RABFA trace (burn-in = first half)") truth <- sim$truth$feature_labels[rownames(m$selected)] table(selected = rowSums(m$selected) > 0, true_signal = truth) #>         true_signal #> selected   0   1 #>    FALSE 163   7 #>    TRUE    4 156 g   <- build_feature_graph(sim$data, cutoff = 0.5, max_neighbors = 5) fit <- rabfa(sim$data, k = 4, graph = g, iter = 5000, burnin = 2500)
